docs.title: NX-OS Family Reference (Beta)
docs.text:
Beta

NX-OS NXOSConfig support is a Beta runtime slice. The schema is v1alpha1, family coverage is still expanding, and wire-format behaviour may change between releases. See Production Readiness for the current scope and hardening roadmap.

Declarative NX-OS device configuration is driven by the NXOSConfig CRD over NX-API REST/DME, using the shared Network as Code config engine. Unlike the IOS-XE Family Reference — which is generated from vendored YANG across many families — the NX-OS slice currently ships a focused set of hand-written family writers.

docs.title: Supported families
docs.text:
Family Key Covers System system Device-level settings such as hostname Feature feature Individual NX-OS feature enablement (e.g. interface-vlan, lacp) Feature set feature_set Installable feature sets (e.g. fex) VLAN vlan VLAN definitions (id, name) Interface (Ethernet) interface_ethernet Ethernet interface config: description, MTU, admin state

The strict NetAsCode path emits the pinned provider's derived Layer-2/admin attributes, but refuses to convert an observed non-Layer-2 interface and requires an explicit shutdown: false before bringing up an observed shutdown port. Native CVK source preserves omitted admin/layer properties.

Each family is opt-in per NXOSConfig via spec.managedFamilies; the engine only reconciles families you list and applies the shared drift-detection contract. NX-OS revision history and rollback are not implemented yet.

For sources that declare modelSource.format: netascode-nxos, feature and feature_set leaves must use the canonical Boolean types. Provider-state strings such as enabled, disabled, installed, or uninstalled remain a native-CVK compatibility extension only and are rejected at the strict import boundary.

docs.title: Device release gate
docs.text:
NX-OS writes fail closed unless the live show version result matches an admitted profile. Admission here means the release can exercise the parity pipeline; it is not production certification of every DME mapping.

Live release pattern Maturity Model contract Evidence 10.3(9) plus an optional alphanumeric, ., _, or - suffix Admitted Beta 0.3.0 CVK Nexus 9000v lab evidence; current automated credentialed run pending 10.5(4) plus an optional alphanumeric, ., _, or - suffix Experimental, explicit opt-in 0.3.0 Upstream NetAsCode tested-version matrix and pinned static DME oracle; CVK live qualification pending

Experimental profiles are rejected by default. A lab operator can opt in to 10.5(4) with Helm value nxos.allowExperimentalReleases=true, which sets CVK_NXOS_ALLOW_EXPERIMENTAL_RELEASES=true on the controller and propagates it to per-device pods. This gate is not a production certification; leave it off until the live write/removal/rollback checklist passes for that release.

An empty version records Ready=False, reason=DeviceVersionPending and is retried automatically. A syntactically invalid result records MalformedDeviceVersion; a well-formed release outside the table records UnsupportedDeviceVersion. Both rejected states remain Pending and cannot reach a writer mutation. If spec.targetYangVersion is set, it must equal the normalized live release profile; it cannot be used to select a different DME shape than the running device.

docs.title: Example
docs.text:
apiVersion: config.cisco.vk/v1alpha1
kind: NXOSConfig
metadata:
  name: nexus9300v-vlans
  namespace: default
spec:
  deviceRef:
    name: nexus9300v-01
  managedFamilies:
    - system
    - vlan
    - interface_ethernet
  driftPolicy: revert
  driftDetectInterval: 5m
  writeStartup: true
  modelSource:
    format: netascode-nxos
    modelVersion: 0.3.0
    schemaDigest: sha256:5d5482679fb28e751d34cdc49342f8434914a7714966ba8244923b95d678698d
    resolved: true
    exporter: example-customer-exporter@0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
    sourceRevision: 0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
  source:
    inline:
      system:
        hostname: nexus9300v-01
      vlan:
        vlans:
          - id: 3903
            name: CVK_LAB
      interfaces:
        ethernets:
          - id: 1/1
            description: CVK lab uplink
            shutdown: false
            mtu: 9216

docs.title: v2026.10.0 release candidate
docs.text:
Target release date: 2026-10-01 Status: unpublished release candidate

Comparison baseline: published v2026.9.2. Release preparation starts from merged main commit 15c14d7d; the final reviewed preparation commit must be recorded in the readiness ledger before tagging.

This page describes the planned October release. It is not a release artifact reference until the tag, images, chart, checksums, and signatures appear on the public Releases page.

docs.title: What changes for operators since September
docs.text:
• Secure IOS-XE gNOI supports password authentication metadata and explicit certificate provisioning for the OS service. Verified TLS and provisioning trust are scoped to gNOI; this is not a global transport or gNMI security bypass. Read-only OS.Verify does not install certificates. See gNOI and Software Lifecycle and the upgrade/downgrade runbook.
  • Devices can project administrator-controlled topology labels into native Kubernetes Nodes. Affinity and topology-spread constraints place eligible application workloads; CVK's rollout controller separately uses frozen topology domains and budgets to order device software changes. Kubernetes scheduling alone does not decide whether a network path is safe to interrupt.
  • IOSXESoftwareRollout provides immutable, approved multi-device plans, canaries, domain/concurrency budgets and topology-specific image sources. This is a combined transfer/activation/recovery workflow, not separately approved durable staging.
  • Managed workers use two functional ServiceAccounts (app-hosting and network-management), with read-only/read-write role options, rather than a ServiceAccount for every device. Admission/worker binding is part of the security boundary; RBAC alone is not per-device authorization.
  • PDB-aware drain remains a disabled-by-default development preview for the documented supported workload subset. It is not general-purpose evacuation or a guarantee of application/network continuity.
  • Dependency updates include OpenTelemetry logging migration and golang.org/x/crypto. CI/lab execution has correlated lifecycle telemetry; that telemetry is diagnostic evidence, not proof of complete qualification.
  • Release preparation updates the documentation website to Next.js 16.3.8 and fixes affected transitive dependencies; see the readiness ledger for audit results and the separate remaining container/security gates.

Merged scope: PRs #184–#188 and #190–#194. No code from the subsequent pr/johalley/tas-extentions November roadmap is included by this preparation.

docs.title: Release scope
docs.text:
The release candidate combines the Kubernetes-native topology foundation with the first IOS-XE rollout capabilities:

  • manager-owned CiscoDevice-to-Node identity and bounded topology projection;
  • native scheduler affinity and topology-spread placement;
  • immutable IOS-XE rollout plans with topology-domain budgets, canaries, and pause/cancel recovery;
  • topology-scoped image endpoint selection with frozen endpoint, digest, and Secret identity per target;
  • secure gNOI transfer, activation, and verification through the existing IOS-XE software lifecycle; and
  • an opt-in, PDB-aware Eviction drain for the explicitly supported workload subset.

The rollout and drain APIs remain alpha/preview contracts. Managed topology, write-class gNOI, and workload drain are disabled by default and require the administrator to opt in after completing the admission and rollback checks in the managed topology guide.

docs.title: Compatibility boundary
docs.text:
• Kubernetes 1.35 is the CVK support floor for managed topology.
  • Kubernetes 1.37 native TAS has a separate experimental scheduler-conformance lane. Fixture scheduler tests do not establish the full physical CVK group lifecycle; TAS is not a CVK runtime dependency or enabled by default.
  • The public rollout implementation in this release is IOS-XE-specific. NX-OS and IOS-XR do not receive a generic rollout API from this release.
  • The physical qualification evidence covers the IOS-XE lab fleet used by the project. It does not establish multi-site fault tolerance, zero-downtime guarantees, or cross-platform production support.

docs.title: Upgrade and rollback
docs.text:
Existing Helm installations must apply all reviewed CRDs from the pinned October chart before the controller upgrade; Helm does not upgrade CRDs. Compared with September, IOSXESoftwareRollout is new and CiscoDevice, IOSXESoftwareUpgrade and IOSXEOperationalAction schemas change. Follow the CRD upgrade procedure, back up both schemas and custom resources, and test stored-object compatibility first.

Keep managed topology, software mutation and drain disabled unless deliberately adopting their qualified scope. Before enabling them, validate native admission, functional-account permissions, exact ownership and the opt-in migration steps in the managed topology guide. Do not overlap old and new workers' device authority or drop guards on unresolved operations.

Rolling back the chart does not roll back schemas, restore discarded fields, or undo a device activation. Never delete CRDs, claims, Leases or retained operation history as a shortcut. Use the documented recovery procedure and verify device/app state separately from Pod readiness.

docs.title: Known qualification limits / publication hold
docs.text: This candidate is not yet approved for tagging. The readiness ledger must link exact-candidate CI, API/admission, migration and physical evidence. Later dirty November-development builds exposed delayed drain callbacks, stale Running Pod cleanup markers and stopped evidence collectors. Those runs neither prove this exact main candidate faulty nor certify it safe. Before publication, reproduce/triage that lifecycle on the October candidate and either qualify a minimal reviewed fix or make an explicit reviewed scope decision; do not silently inherit November fixes or declare preview drain production-qualified. Independent endpoint/forwarding continuity remains unproven, and unsupported package/storage/signing cases must stay explicit.

docs.title: Required release gates
docs.text:
The release candidate must be cut from the final merged commit, not from an intermediate stacked branch. Before tagging, maintainers must record passing results for:

  1. go test ./... and go test -race ./...;
  2. go vet ./..., build, and go mod verify;
  3. generated deepcopy/CRD/RBAC parity and Helm lint/render checks;
  4. the Kubernetes 1.35 real-API admission and default-scheduler suite;
  5. secure gNOI upgrade and downgrade validation on the supported IOS-XE lab devices, including final Node, Pod, PDB, Lease, reservation, and device inventory evidence;
  6. strict documentation build; and
  7. vulnerability and dependency checks on the exact release commit.

Do not publish while a release check is failing or while a dependency update has an unresolved vulnerability result. A failed dependency PR must be fixed or explicitly deferred in the release decision; it must not be merged merely to unblock the feature stack.

docs.title: Operational expectations
docs.text:
The supported upgrade path is a controlled relocation protocol. It protects eligible Pods with Kubernetes Eviction and PDB semantics, waits for the exact post-termination device inventory evidence, and releases the protection only after the manager's fencing Lease and worker observations are settled. It is not a promise of uninterrupted network forwarding or zero downtime.

Operators should retain the following evidence for every production change:

  • the applied rollout and approval manifests;
  • campaign and per-device phase transitions;
  • CVK manager and worker logs with secret material redacted;
  • IOS-XE console and show command evidence;
  • final topology, Node, Pod, PDB, Lease, and reservation state; and
  • the exact image digest and source endpoint selected for each target.

docs.title: Deferred roadmap
docs.text:
The following work is intentionally outside this release:

  • durable image prefetch, shared cache, and cache-loss recovery;
  • independently durable install/stage/activate reservations and resumable activation;
  • general-purpose workload evacuation for StatefulSets, DaemonSets, Jobs, PVC-backed workloads, or custom controllers;
  • an authoritative discovered topology graph or graph-cost scheduler;
  • mandatory native Workload/PodGroup/TAS integration;
  • generic NX-OS or IOS-XR rollout APIs;
  • multi-cluster ownership and cross-controller fencing; and
  • automated routing, forwarding, utilization, and critical-service health gates.

The shipped behavior is documented in the topology guide. The separately preserved November handoff and roadmap tracks future implementation and testing; it is not part of October qualification.

November builds on October's app hosting, managed topology and secure IOS-XE software workflows. It adds staged software activation, bounded topology extensions and two Alpha controller adapters, with clearer documentation for platform engineers, network operators, security reviewers and contributors.

docs.title: A simpler documentation path
docs.text:
The dynamic website introduces app hosting, configuration and operations through short explanations and diagrams. MkDocs separates how CVK works, deployment guides, operations and technical reference.

Managed topology, Security and Operations now have short overviews and focused task pages. Existing section links remain usable. The content distinguishes application placement from device operating-system changes, and corrects credential, permission and runtime claims against the implementation.

docs.title: Staged IOS-XE maintenance and topology extensions
docs.text:
October already included managed topology and IOSXESoftwareRollout. November extends that opt-in workflow with:

  • PrepareOnly and durable preparation receipts, followed by separately approved, receipt-bound activation;
  • accepted network observations, claim-time checks and health checks through recovery, with administrator disruption protections and overlapping risk budgets;
  • bounded image-transfer pacing, read-only accepted-topology diagnostics and additional protocol, drain and ownership-recovery safeguards; and
  • validated, revision-bound public device-HTTPS CA projection through spec.tls.caSecretRef.

Start with the topology overview, then choose application scheduling or the IOS-XE campaign procedure. Read the recovery procedure before changing retained ownership. The bounded implementation scope records the qualification limits; it is not evidence for a different release candidate.

docs.title: Controller adapters — Alpha
docs.text:
Catalyst SD-WAN: native reconciliation of supported controller intent, configuration verification and ownership tracking, without a Terraform runtime dependency. Coverage is fixture-qualified and does not imply full model parity or general live attachment/activation qualification. Remote prune/import and ownership release remain restricted; use the supported Retain behavior. See the SD-WAN guide and qualification backlog.

Nexus Dashboard: controller health, version and paginated inventory, with optional adoption of reachable NX-OS switches as CiscoDevice resources. Adoption is disabled by default; removal defaults to Retain. The adapter does not manage Nexus Dashboard configuration. Production-size pagination and multi-fabric operation need additional qualification before opting into pruning. See the Nexus Dashboard guide.

docs.title: Runtime and dependency maintenance
docs.text:
• Virtual Kubelet advances from 1.12.0 to 1.14.1, with Go 1.26.10 and controller-runtime 0.25.2. Kubernetes client libraries advance to the 0.37 series; this does not change the managed-topology server floor below.
  • Managed workers preserve their reachable Pod-IP kubelet endpoint on port 10250, while the manager retains ownership of protected Node identity.
  • The documentation stack includes Next.js 16.4.3 and Mermaid 12.2.0, with updated math rendering and dependency/browser-runtime license bundles. Security scans remain required on the actual candidate and staged images.

docs.title: Upgrade from October
docs.text:
Use chart 2026.11.0 and image v2026.11.0 together after publication. Before upgrading, save the current Helm values, CRD definitions and custom-resource instances. Read the installation maintenance guide.

  1. Review the complete CRD directory from the signed November chart. Existing CiscoDevice, NetworkController, IOSXESoftwareRollout and IOSXESoftwareUpgrade schemas have substantive changes; other generated CRD manifests are refreshed. There is no new CRD kind in this delta.
  2. Apply all reviewed chart CRDs and wait for them to be Established before upgrading the controller. Helm does not upgrade CRDs automatically.
  3. Keep CRDs, chart, admission policies, manager and workers matched. Preserve prior gate settings while validating migration. Review unresolved claims, active campaigns and prepared receipts before the maintenance window; do not overlap migration with disruptive device work.
  4. Follow the managed enablement and identity-handoff procedure where applicable. A combined-to-split worker migration requires a live Helm upgrade; do not substitute pruning of retained identities or policy objects.
  5. Verify manager and worker readiness, device conditions, existing application health and controller-adapter permissions before enabling new capabilities.

The APIs remain v1alpha1. A Helm rollback does not restore stored objects, undo OS activation or authorize an older manager to consume newer protocol state. Do not remove Leases, claims, finalizers or receipts to bypass a block. Use the recovery and retirement guide.

docs.title: Compatibility and known limits
docs.text:
• Managed topology requires Kubernetes 1.35+ and its documented native admission and functional ServiceAccount controls. It remains disabled by default; network management starts read-only. Software mutation and drain require explicit opt-in.
  • PDB-aware drain remains a disabled-by-default development preview, with limited workload eligibility. The recorded physical cohort does not establish service-through-reload, multi-site fault tolerance or a zero-downtime guarantee.
  • Native TAS is a separate experimental Kubernetes 1.37 lane. It is not a baseline dependency or full physical grouped-workload qualification; grouped drain remains unsupported.
  • IOS-XE software campaigns do not provide generic NX-OS or IOS-XR rollouts. NX-OS app hosting and configuration remain Beta. Controller adapters remain Alpha; adapters absent from this release are not enabled by adding a CRD.
  • Hosted-app logs, exec, attach and port-forward remain unsupported through the VK kubelet API. Worker logs and supported device diagnostics remain available. Device metrics do not provide per-Pod CPU/memory usage.
  • App-hosting identities still need cluster-wide workload Secret reads. Separate namespaces and cache filters do not eliminate that exposure. Review the authorization boundary and TLS/credential guides.

See feature availability for the full maturity table. Existing lab records apply only to their recorded source, platform and test conditions. They do not certify the final November candidate.

docs.title: Release authorization and verification
docs.text:
One normal current-head Approve review from an eligible maintainer other than the release operator is sufficient under the release policy. No prescribed review comment or separate draft approval is required. All branch checks, candidate qualification, vulnerability gates and staged-artifact verification still apply.

The November preparation record separates preparation checks from final publication evidence. The GitHub Release is published only after staging and verification pass. Signed image/chart tags may already be public during staging; their existence does not mean the release is approved for use. The websites build from the exact published tag.

docs.title: Corrected November release preparation record
docs.text:
Prepared 29 October 2026 for proposed v2026.11.1. The original November release target date was 1 November 2026. Previous published baseline: v2026.10.0. Correction base: PR #210 merge 089c5c4a2f13e09c2b1ef462da230841184a30f5.

This is a reviewable correction, not a declaration of publication, approval or final qualification. The new protected preparation PR must record its current approval, final merged SHA and verification evidence. Do not reuse the old candidate's approval or artifact results as approval of changed source/version.

docs.title: Why the previous candidate was rejected
docs.text:
v2026.11.0 was tagged and staged, but exact inspection of its linux/arm64 controller image found the MPL-labelled scalar-parcels.json and classic-templates.json embedded in the executable without corresponding copied source or attribution in /licenses. The inspected image digest was sha256:3426c740728aaa4b34ace434b9f4e62f1a5ccca2c838032a2146a3b8a83c94d2.

That failed the existing Licensing is a hard gate requirement. The original notes and preparation record remain historical. Never publish that draft, move/delete the tag, or replace its staged artifacts. October remains the published baseline. This was an artifact packaging finding; it does not change the recorded platform qualification.

docs.title: Proposed correction and retained scope
docs.text:
• Canonical v2026.11.1 notes retain the November scope compared with October: bounded topology extensions, SD-WAN and Nexus Dashboard Alpha adapters, runtime/dependency updates and the documentation redesign.
  • The minimal functional change is image packaging: explicitly include linked embedded source, license text, attribution and provenance in /licenses/embedded-source/, with a manifest and byte-comparison checks. SD-WAN definitions and the applicable IOS-XE model/schema source retain their repository-relative paths under source/. Existing Go license checks remain.
  • Current selectors and source chart appVersion target v2026.11.1. Source chart version: 0.1.0 remains the development default; tag automation stamps packaged chart 2026.11.1. Historical candidates are not renumbered.
  • The approved website wording/design and the November feature maturity, runtime gates, qualification limits and migration boundaries are retained. No new runtime behavior or deferred feature is included by this correction.
  • The release runbook targets the corrected candidate and October baseline. It preserves normal current-head approval, draft-before-tag, immutable artifacts and publication-only documentation deployment.

docs.title: Verification and publication gates
docs.text:
Record the new candidate's local checks and remote results in its preparation PR. Checks on PR #210 and the rejected staged image do not qualify new artifacts. Do not change frozen source solely to record final bookkeeping here.

Gate Required evidence for v2026.11.1 Protected correction PR Normal current-head approval from an eligible maintainer other than the release operator; all current branch rules and required checks pass. Changed version/source/notes require the new review. Required checks build-and-smoke, ygot-validate, terraform-provider, govulncheck, helm4-compat, lab-ci-next / cat8kv, and lab-ci-next / cat9k on the qualifying candidate; re-read protection for changes. Packaging regression Embedded-source helper tests; target-specific linked-input inventory; byte-identical source, LICENSE/README, provenance and generator copies in both image bundles. Candidate verification Applicable Go/race/vet, generated CRD/RBAC parity, real-API/admission/scheduler, chart/install/October-upgrade/rollback and device checks under the existing runbook. Prior records apply only to their named revision and scope. Security and licensing Required vulnerability scans, dependency audits, existing Go/website/MkDocs license checks, and exact staged-image inspection of /licenses/embedded-source/ against frozen source. SBOMs supplement redistribution verification. Draft and staging Approved frozen merge SHA, signing identity and rendered canonical notes; exactly one unpublished draft before a new signed tag; all 16 allowlisted assets staged successfully. Independent artifact verification Image/chart/plugin signatures, provenance, checksums, platform execution, package contents and image aliases from the exact corrected candidate. Publication and distribution Publish only after the corrected release is authorized and all gates pass; then verify immutable release, tag-based docs and the normal Krew update.

The correction does not waive or narrow release gates. No prescribed review comment, separate draft-ID approval or extra reviewer task is introduced.

docs.title: Operator sequence
docs.text:
1. Review and merge the correction PR after its current required checks pass.
  2. Freeze that exact merged source and record the new normal review and authorization for v2026.11.1. Preparing this PR does not tag or publish it.
  3. Follow the runbook to verify the candidate, render these committed notes, create its new draft, then push its new signed tag. Do not reuse the rejected candidate's draft, tag, assets or success record.
  4. Inspect all staging outputs and independently compare the embedded source bundle with the frozen candidate. Publish only after all required gates pass.
  5. If further source or artifact changes are needed after tagging, leave the failed candidate unpublished and prepare v2026.11.2. Never move an existing tag or replace its artifacts.

docs.title: Cisco Virtual Kubelet v2026.11.1
docs.text:
Proposed corrected November candidate. The original release target date was 1 November 2026. Comparison baseline: published v2026.10.0. The GitHub release page is the authority for publication status and signed artifacts. Until it is public, use the published October release; preparation notes do not make an artifact available.

v2026.11.0 was tagged and staged from preparation PR #210 but was rejected before publication because exact artifact inspection found an incomplete embedded-source/attribution bundle. It remains an immutable, unpublished recovery marker; never publish its draft or replace its artifacts. This candidate retains the original November scope below and adds the packaging correction described next. See the rejected-candidate record.

November builds on October's app hosting, managed topology and secure IOS-XE software workflows. It adds staged software activation, bounded topology extensions and two Alpha controller adapters, with clearer documentation for platform engineers, network operators, security reviewers and contributors.

docs.title: Corrected embedded-source and attribution packaging
docs.text:
The correction adds an explicit embedded-source bundle to the controller and config-lint images. /licenses/embedded-source/ contains a manifest and repository-relative copies under source/, including the linked SD-WAN JSON definitions, their MPL license and provenance, and applicable IOS-XE generated model/schema sources and Cisco attribution. The existing Go dependency license bundle remains in place.

Packaging checks compare expected source and attribution bytes and reject missing or changed files. Inspect the exact staged images independently before publication; source availability in GitHub or a passing SBOM inventory alone does not satisfy the redistribution gate. This correction changes packaging and release metadata, without expanding device behavior, adapter qualification or the feature maturity described below.

docs.title: A simpler documentation path
docs.text:
The dynamic website introduces app hosting, configuration and operations through short explanations and diagrams. MkDocs separates how CVK works, deployment guides, operations and technical reference.

Managed topology, Security and Operations now have short overviews and focused task pages. Existing section links remain usable. The content distinguishes application placement from device operating-system changes, and corrects credential, permission and runtime claims against the implementation.

docs.title: Staged IOS-XE maintenance and topology extensions
docs.text:
October already included managed topology and IOSXESoftwareRollout. November extends that opt-in workflow with:

  • PrepareOnly and durable preparation receipts, followed by separately approved, receipt-bound activation;
  • accepted network observations, claim-time checks and health checks through recovery, with administrator disruption protections and overlapping risk budgets;
  • bounded image-transfer pacing, read-only accepted-topology diagnostics and additional protocol, drain and ownership-recovery safeguards; and
  • validated, revision-bound public device-HTTPS CA projection through spec.tls.caSecretRef.

Start with the topology overview, then choose application scheduling or the IOS-XE campaign procedure. Read the recovery procedure before changing retained ownership. The bounded implementation scope records the qualification limits; it is not evidence for a different release candidate.

docs.title: Controller adapters — Alpha
docs.text:
Catalyst SD-WAN: native reconciliation of supported controller intent, configuration verification and ownership tracking, without a Terraform runtime dependency. Coverage is fixture-qualified and does not imply full model parity or general live attachment/activation qualification. Remote prune/import and ownership release remain restricted; use the supported Retain behavior. See the SD-WAN guide and qualification backlog.

Nexus Dashboard: controller health, version and paginated inventory, with optional adoption of reachable NX-OS switches as CiscoDevice resources. Adoption is disabled by default; removal defaults to Retain. The adapter does not manage Nexus Dashboard configuration. Production-size pagination and multi-fabric operation need additional qualification before opting into pruning. See the Nexus Dashboard guide.

docs.title: Runtime and dependency maintenance
docs.text:
• Virtual Kubelet advances from 1.12.0 to 1.14.1, with Go 1.26.10 and controller-runtime 0.25.2. Kubernetes client libraries advance to the 0.37 series; this does not change the managed-topology server floor below.
  • Managed workers preserve their reachable Pod-IP kubelet endpoint on port 10250, while the manager retains ownership of protected Node identity.
  • The documentation stack includes Next.js 16.4.3 and Mermaid 12.2.0, with updated math rendering and dependency/browser-runtime license bundles. Security scans remain required on the actual candidate and staged images.

docs.title: Upgrade from October
docs.text:
Use chart 2026.11.1 and image v2026.11.1 together after publication. Before upgrading, save the current Helm values, CRD definitions and custom-resource instances. Read the installation maintenance guide.

  1. Review the complete CRD directory from the signed November chart. Existing CiscoDevice, NetworkController, IOSXESoftwareRollout and IOSXESoftwareUpgrade schemas have substantive changes; other generated CRD manifests are refreshed. There is no new CRD kind in this delta.
  2. Apply all reviewed chart CRDs and wait for them to be Established before upgrading the controller. Helm does not upgrade CRDs automatically.
  3. Keep CRDs, chart, admission policies, manager and workers matched. Preserve prior gate settings while validating migration. Review unresolved claims, active campaigns and prepared receipts before the maintenance window; do not overlap migration with disruptive device work.
  4. Follow the managed enablement and identity-handoff procedure where applicable. A combined-to-split worker migration requires a live Helm upgrade; do not substitute pruning of retained identities or policy objects.
  5. Verify manager and worker readiness, device conditions, existing application health and controller-adapter permissions before enabling new capabilities.

The APIs remain v1alpha1. A Helm rollback does not restore stored objects, undo OS activation or authorize an older manager to consume newer protocol state. Do not remove Leases, claims, finalizers or receipts to bypass a block. Use the recovery and retirement guide.

docs.title: Compatibility and known limits
docs.text:
• Managed topology requires Kubernetes 1.35+ and its documented native admission and functional ServiceAccount controls. It remains disabled by default; network management starts read-only. Software mutation and drain require explicit opt-in.
  • PDB-aware drain remains a disabled-by-default development preview, with limited workload eligibility. The recorded physical cohort does not establish service-through-reload, multi-site fault tolerance or a zero-downtime guarantee.
  • Native TAS is a separate experimental Kubernetes 1.37 lane. It is not a baseline dependency or full physical grouped-workload qualification; grouped drain remains unsupported.
  • IOS-XE software campaigns do not provide generic NX-OS or IOS-XR rollouts. NX-OS app hosting and configuration remain Beta. Controller adapters remain Alpha; adapters absent from this release are not enabled by adding a CRD.
  • Hosted-app logs, exec, attach and port-forward remain unsupported through the VK kubelet API. Worker logs and supported device diagnostics remain available. Device metrics do not provide per-Pod CPU/memory usage.
  • App-hosting identities still need cluster-wide workload Secret reads. Separate namespaces and cache filters do not eliminate that exposure. Review the authorization boundary and TLS/credential guides.

See feature availability for the full maturity table. Existing lab records apply only to their recorded source, platform and test conditions. They do not certify the final November candidate.

docs.title: Release authorization and verification
docs.text:
One normal current-head Approve review from an eligible maintainer other than the release operator is sufficient under the release policy. No prescribed review comment or separate draft approval is required. All branch checks, candidate qualification, vulnerability gates and staged-artifact verification still apply.

The November preparation record separates preparation checks from final publication evidence. The GitHub Release is published only after staging and verification pass. Signed image/chart tags may already be public during staging; their existence does not mean the release is approved for use. The websites build from the exact published tag.

docs.title: v2026.9.0 — unpublished candidate
docs.text:
The signed v2026.9.0 tag triggered the release workflow on 2026-09-01, but the workflow stopped in its draft-visibility preflight. No controller image, Helm chart, kubectl plugin archive, SBOM, signature, provenance, or other release asset was built, pushed, signed, staged, or published by that run.

The immutable tag remains as release-history evidence and will not be moved or deleted. Its GitHub draft has zero attached assets and will not be published. No Krew update was triggered for this candidate; at the time, the official index remained at v2026.8.1. Do not use v2026.9.0 installation URLs or version selectors.

The preflight permission correction was first carried by the also-unpublished v2026.9.1 security candidate. The complete, remediated September product update is carried by v2026.9.2, whose product delta is measured from the last official release, v2026.8.1.

docs.title: v2026.9.1 — unpublished security candidate
docs.text:
Candidate build date: 2026-09-01

The signed v2026.9.1 tag completed the release workflow, staged the expected 16-asset draft, and pushed signed controller-image and OCI-chart tags. During the required pre-publication review, the release-image scan reported two versioned dependency findings for which fixes were available:

  • CRITICAL CVE-2026-56854 in golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0, fixed in v0.55.0.
  • HIGH CVE-2026-46600 in golang.org/x/net v0.55.0, fixed in v0.56.0.

Symbol-aware govulncheck found no reachable vulnerable call path in the controller: the reported SSH path is server-only while CVK uses SSH client APIs, and the reported DNS message symbols are not called. Even so, maintainers made a no-go decision because a release with fixed HIGH/CRITICAL dependency findings should not be published.

The immutable tag and draft are retained as release-history evidence and will not be moved, deleted, or published. No release: published event occurred, so no documentation deployment or Krew update was triggered for v2026.9.1. Do not use its image, chart, draft assets, download URLs, or installation selectors.

The older workflow emitted the mutable 2026.9 and latest image aliases before its advisory scan, so those aliases can temporarily resolve to this unpublished candidate during recovery. Do not advertise or use them, and do not rerun the v2026.9.1 tag workflow: a rerun could move the aliases again outside the corrected release gates. The v2026.9.2 workflow replaces them only after both image platforms and the complete staged candidate pass.

The remediated September release is v2026.9.2. Its product delta remains measured from the last official release, v2026.8.1.

docs.title: v2026.9.2 release notes
docs.text:
Release date: 2026-09-01

Availability: Use this release only when v2026.9.2 appears on the public Releases page. If it is not listed there, the candidate has not been published and its tag, image, chart, and download URLs must not be used.

Recovery from the unpublished September candidates: The signed v2026.9.0 workflow stopped in draft-visibility preflight before it built or staged any artifact. The corrected v2026.9.1 workflow completed, staged the expected 16 draft assets, and pushed signed image and OCI chart tags, but its pre-publication image scan found fixed HIGH/CRITICAL dependency findings. Maintainers therefore made a no-go decision. Neither draft was published, and neither candidate triggered documentation deployment or a Krew update. Their immutable tags will not be moved or deleted. v2026.9.2 contains the dependency remediation and is the replacement September release; its product delta is measured from the last official release, v2026.8.1.

This update adds an Alpha controller-extension foundation and inspectable controller build identity, and strengthens source installation, release provenance, vulnerability gating, and redistributed licensing. It retains the existing IOS-XE, NX-OS, credential-rotation, telemetry, operations, and software lifecycle functionality from v2026.8.1.

docs.title: In plain English: what is new since v2026.8.1
docs.text:
• You get two new Kubernetes CRD contracts and the manager scaffold needed for future external-controller integrations. You do not get a working Catalyst Center, APIC, Meraki, or other controller adapter in this release.
  • IOS-XE and NX-OS device behavior is unchanged. Automatic rollout after a referenced credential Secret changes already existed in v2026.8.1; this release documents that behavior and its security boundary more clearly.
  • The dependencies implicated by the rejected v2026.9.1 image findings are upgraded, and both controller-image architectures now have hard HIGH/CRITICAL vulnerability gates before merge and during release.
  • Controller and plugin version reporting, reproducible packaging, signing, provenance checks, and redistributed license material are more strictly verified. These changes make the same deliverables easier to inspect and trust; they do not add new device commands.
  • The release publishes rebuilt v2026.9.2 plugin archives. After publication, automation opens the normal upstream Krew index update PR; Krew users receive v2026.9.2 only after that PR merges. The plugin's commands and supported platforms are unchanged.
  • Existing Helm installations must apply the two new CRDs before upgrading. Fresh installations receive them from the chart automatically.

docs.title: Alpha network-controller extension foundation
docs.text:
Two new namespaced CRDs establish a generic boundary for future external controller integrations:

  • NetworkController (cisco.vk/v1alpha1) declares an HTTPS endpoint, adapter type, credential and trust references, connection limits, and administrator-approved intent Secret aliases.
  • NetworkControllerConfig (config.cisco.vk/v1alpha1) carries resolved, explicitly versioned controller-centric Network as Code intent, managed sections, ownership, and policy.

The manager includes adapter registration contracts, duplicate-endpoint fencing, isolated per-endpoint worker orchestration, material-rotation handling, and fail-closed validation. These are extension contracts, not a product integration: the v2026.9.2 image contains zero product adapters and cannot contact or mutate an external controller. The shipped boundary is report-only; apply, prune, remote-delete behavior, and mutation RBAC remain unimplemented.

See the Network Controller Extension Guide and CRD Reference.

docs.title: Existing device-credential rollout clarified
docs.text:
This rollout behavior is not new in v2026.9.2: v2026.8.1 already watched referenced credential Secrets. Updating a Secret referenced by CiscoDevice.spec.credentialSecretRef causes the manager to update the pod-template cisco.vk/credential-resource-version annotation and roll every affected VK Deployment. An explicit kubectl rollout restart is no longer part of the normal credential-rotation path.

This release clarifies the security boundary around that existing behavior. The manager observes a typed Secret object's resourceVersion; reconciliation does not inspect .data, but Secret data can still enter the manager's cache/API client. The manager's Secret RBAC and memory therefore remain in the credential trust boundary. See Bulk rotation and Security principles.

docs.title: Dependency remediation and hard vulnerability gates
docs.text:
• The controller moves from golang.org/x/crypto v0.52.0 to v0.55.0 and selects golang.org/x/net v0.57.0. The separate Terraform helper moves from golang.org/x/net v0.55.0 to the fixed v0.56.0.
  • These updates remediate the versioned dependencies reported for CVE-2026-56854 and CVE-2026-46600 in the unpublished v2026.9.1 image. Symbol-aware govulncheck found no reachable vulnerable call path in that candidate, but maintainers declined to publish while fixed HIGH/CRITICAL dependencies remained.
  • The required pre-merge controller-image scans and the exact tagged-image scans now fail on any fixed HIGH/CRITICAL finding on either Linux AMD64 or ARM64. This supplements the existing symbol-aware controller and Terraform govulncheck gates. Mutable 2026.9 and latest image aliases move only after both platform scans and all chart, plugin, and curated-draft staging complete successfully.

docs.title: Verifiable build identity and distribution hardening
docs.text:
• Release-built cisco-vk version and cisco-vk --version report the exact release tag, full source commit, and reproducible RFC3339 UTC build time. Direct development builds identify themselves as devel.
  • The existing Linux AMD64/ARM64 non-root controller images now use a pinned Go 1.26.7 builder and digest-pinned builder/runtime bases, use reproducible build flags, and redistribute the project, dependency, Go toolchain, NOTICE, and patent material applicable to their binaries.
  • The existing plugin archives remain available for Linux and macOS on AMD64 and ARM64. They now include applicable Go license/patent files and undergo exact archive installation and execution checks through Krew; Windows remains unsupported.
  • Signed image, chart, checksum, plugin, SBOM, and provenance artifacts already existed in v2026.8.1. This release strengthens their immutable tool pins, draft/asset checks, and pre- and post-publication verification.
  • The source installer now checksum-verifies Linux AMD64/ARM64 Go downloads, installs a private versioned toolchain without replacing /usr/local/go, and limits itself to building and installing the binary. It no longer tries to create TLS files or a systemd unit; Helm remains the supported cluster installation path.
  • Documentation build dependencies and browser assets are pinned and license-checked. The website dependency updates include the nanoid 3.3.18 security fix. Generated IOS-XE family-page additions document fields that the runtime already supported; they do not add device behavior.

See the CLI and plugin reference, Getting Started, and the project licensing summary.

docs.title: Required upgrade action: apply both new CRDs first
docs.text:
Helm installs files under crds/ on a fresh installation but does not apply new or updated CRDs during helm upgrade. An existing installation must apply the NetworkController and NetworkControllerConfig CRDs before upgrading.

After the release is published:

kubectl apply --server-side -f \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cisco-open/cisco-virtual-kubelet/v2026.9.2/config/crd/cisco.vk_networkcontrollers.yaml
kubectl apply --server-side -f \
  https://raw.githubusercontent.com/cisco-open/cisco-virtual-kubelet/v2026.9.2/config/crd/config.cisco.vk_networkcontrollerconfigs.yaml

kubectl wait --for=condition=Established --timeout=60s \
  crd/networkcontrollers.cisco.vk \
  crd/networkcontrollerconfigs.config.cisco.vk

helm upgrade cvk \
  oci://ghcr.io/cisco-open/charts/cisco-virtual-kubelet \
  --version 2026.9.2 \
  --namespace cvk-system \
  --reuse-values --wait --timeout 5m

kubectl rollout restart \
  deployment/cvk-cisco-virtual-kubelet-controller \
  --namespace cvk-system
kubectl rollout status \
  deployment/cvk-cisco-virtual-kubelet-controller \
  --namespace cvk-system --timeout=5m

If either new CRD is absent when the new manager first starts, existing CiscoDevice reconcilers continue running, but NetworkController registration is disabled for that process. Apply the CRDs and restart the manager to enable the Alpha scaffold. The restart does not add a product adapter or enable external-controller mutations.

For a release name other than cvk, resolve the controller Deployment from its Helm labels instead of copying the example name. See Upgrading CRDs for the complete procedure and rollback cautions.

docs.title: Compatibility and security notes
docs.text:
• Source builds require Go 1.26.7 or a later 1.26 patch, or Go 1.27.0 or a later 1.27 patch. The release build is pinned to Go 1.26.7.
  • Chart users need Helm 3.21+ or 4.2+. The release is validated with exact Helm 3.21.4 and 4.2.4 binaries.
  • The two new CRDs use CEL transition rules for immutable identity fields. Kubernetes 1.29 or later supports this behavior as GA. On Kubernetes 1.28, CustomResourceValidationExpressions must remain enabled.
  • Controller workers use namespace-scoped RBAC and caches. Endpoints or config authors that do not trust one another should use separate namespaces.
  • Duplicate fencing compares the exact stored endpoint string only within one namespace; it does not normalize equivalent URLs or coordinate across namespaces or clusters.
  • Network-controller credentials and intent values are projected into a worker by the kubelet. The Alpha runtime must not emit desired or observed values in status, events, or logs.
  • No IOS-XE YANG source or generated schema source changed from v2026.8.1. The existing generated material retains its recorded upstream provenance and applicable licensing notices.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• No Catalyst Center, APIC, Meraki, or other product adapter ships in this release. NetworkController and NetworkControllerConfig alone are not a usable controller integration.
  • Network-controller apply, prune, and remote-delete operations are reserved for future gated implementations. The current foundation is report-only.
  • Helm upgrades require the explicit CRD application and manager restart described above. Helm rollback does not remove CRDs or stored custom resources.
  • The kubectl plugin's ad-hoc exec command is IOS-XE-only, read-only, and requires the per-device deployment mode. Windows plugin archives are not produced.
  • NX-OS, device configuration, operational actions, software lifecycle, and telemetry surfaces retain the maturity levels documented in Feature Maturity; their v1alpha1 APIs may continue to evolve.
